newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's GIAT to sell Herstal to Colt's.
newsitem.headline: France's GIAT to sell Herstal to Colt's.

text.p: France's state-owned armaments group GIAT Industries said in a statement it had signed a letter of intent concerning the possible sale of its 92 percent stake in Belgium's Herstal SA to Colt's Manufacturing Company of the United States.

The statement said the deal was conditional on negotiations with Belgium's Walloon region, which has the other eight percent in Herstal, on an industrial plan. These talks are expected to be finalised in September.
Privately owned Colt's said the acquisition would allow it to make the world's biggest group of small calibre arms, uniting four top brands -- Colt, FN Hertsal, Winchester and Browning.
The Walloon region said they hoped the deal would allow Herstal's research and development activities to remain in Liege. GIAT said it hoped the deal would lead to the financial recovery of Herstal.

Herstal was founded in 1889 in Liege near the Dutch border and has a strong position on the military market with FN Herstal and on the hunting and amateur shooting market with Browning and Winchester.
Colt's was founded in 1836 in Hartford, Connecticut by Samuel Colt. It is currently controlled by investment group Zilkha.
